title: Unverified Claim That Robert Maxwell Aided Mogilevich's Passport and Banking Network
description_short: Unverified TrumpFile allegation that Robert Maxwell helped Mogilevich obtain passports and banking access.
description_medium: TrumpFile’s timeline alleges that Robert Maxwell arranged Israeli passports for Semion Mogilevich and 23 associates in 1988, opened a Bank of New York account used for laundering, and connected Mogilevich with KGB chief Vladimir Kryuchkov. An FBI report dated August 1996 instead names Shabtai Kalmanovich in connection with passport access. Neither source independently establishes Maxwell’s alleged role or a relationship to Donald Trump.
description_long: TrumpFile labels this account “Robert Maxwell obtains passports for Mogilevich, helps KGB” and dates its timeline item July 1, 1988. The page’s narrative says the alleged passport arrangement happened “sometime in 1988,” and alleges that Maxwell obtained Israeli passports for Semion Mogilevich and 23 associates, set up a Bank of New York account for money laundering, and introduced Mogilevich to KGB chief Vladimir Kryuchkov. These are claims made by TrumpFile, not independently verified findings. A separately accessed text extraction of an FBI report dated August 1996 says Israeli passports had been obtained by Shabtai Kalmanovich for members of organized-crime groups including the Mogilevich organization. That report does not establish Maxwell’s alleged role, the Bank of New York account, or the KGB connection; its reference to Kalmanovich also cautions against treating TrumpFile’s attribution as confirmed. No passport, bank, court, or contemporaneous record confirming Maxwell’s role is supplied. The packet also provides no link between this 1988 allegation and Donald Trump. This internal draft preserves what the supplied timeline alleges while leaving its date at year-level precision and marking the event unverified; the exact day, related outcomes, and asserted Trump relevance remain unresolved.

title: Kushner's Initial SF-86 Omitted Foreign-Government Contacts
description_short: Kushner's initial SF-86 omitted foreign-government contacts; the 100+ figure was reported later.
description_medium: Jared Kushner’s initial SF-86 was submitted on January 18, 2017, and omitted foreign-government contacts, according to his later statement and his lawyer’s comments to Politico. He said supplemental information followed the next day. The figure of more than 100 contacts was reported in July 2017, so it does not belong to the record’s May 25 date.
description_long: Jared Kushner submitted his initial SF-86 security questionnaire on January 18, 2017. In a July statement to the Senate Judiciary Committee, he said the filing was a rough draft submitted prematurely after his assistant misunderstood a message; the form did not list any foreign-government contacts. He said supplemental information was sent the next day. His explanation is attributed to him and does not independently establish why the form was incomplete. On July 16, Politico quoted Kushner’s attorney Jamie Gorelick saying the original submission omitted all contacts with foreign-government officials and that later materials included more than 100 calls or meetings with representatives of more than 20 countries. That later figure should not be assigned to the May 25 date in the source record: it was reported in July, months after the initial form. This repair dates the event to the January 18 filing and places the 100+ figure in the later supplementation context. The available material establishes the omission and reported correction, but not deliberate concealment, any particular clearance outcome, or the original synopsis’s suggestion that the contacts materially affected the FBI counterintelligence inquiry.

title: Trump Reinstates Schedule F as Schedule Policy/Career
description_short: Trump's January 20, 2025 executive order reinstated Schedule F under the name Schedule Policy/Career.
description_medium: On January 20, 2025, Donald Trump signed an executive order immediately reinstating the 2020 Schedule F order and renaming the category “Schedule Policy/Career.” The order directed the Office of Personnel Management to amend regulations and issue guidance on additional positions for agencies to consider. It establishes a federal workforce policy directive; it does not show how many employees were later reclassified or removed.
description_long: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump signed “Restoring Accountability to Policy-Influencing Positions Within the Federal Workforce.” Section 2 immediately reinstated Executive Order 13957, the 2020 order creating Schedule F, subject to amendments in the new order. Those amendments replaced the excepted-service schedule label “F” with “Policy/Career” and directed the Office of Personnel Management to amend regulations that could impede implementation. The order also directed OPM to issue, within 30 days, guidance about additional position categories agencies should consider recommending for inclusion. It says employees in or applicants for these positions need not personally or politically support the President, but are required to faithfully implement administration policies; failure to do so is grounds for dismissal. These are the signed order’s rules and directions. The accessed document does not establish how many positions were later reclassified, how many employees lost protections, or whether any specific person was dismissed under it. This record describes the enacted policy mechanism, not a completed workforce purge or an asserted list of political enemies.
